A kernel-based root solution for Android
Choose the language used by the app
Files this app staged in the shared temp directory

The app cannot list /data/local/tmp from its own context - the directory allows a traversal, not a read - so the names it knows are stat\'d by name. When a shell answers, the directory is listed through it as well, so a name this app does not write cannot be missed. Any app on the device can see all of it, which is how a detector finds it.
Checked %1$d paths; %2$d could not be read at all.

This deletes every entry in /data/local/tmp, including the %1$d that this app did not stage. Nothing in there is needed by a run that has finished.
%1$d could not be deleted; they are still listed above.

These are in /data/local/tmp and are not this app\'s staging. They are shown because a detector reading the same directory sees them too, and the app will not delete them.
This app\'s own context cannot see into /data/local/tmp on this device, so nothing can be said about what is there - this is a blind reading, not an empty one.

The pipe page budget the exploit needs is spent for this boot. A restart refills it; waiting does not, and every attempt until then fails the same way.
Retrying here is not offered: this boot\'s pipe page budget is spent, and only a restart refills it.
The kernel refused the payload the pipe pages it needs. That budget is spent for this boot, so every attempt from here fails the same way until the phone restarts.

Retrying here is not offered: the last payload may still be running, and a second one on top of it is how a phone locks up.
